findings.description: `gitDirIdentity` now includes `birthtimeMs`. On a Linux host where Node falls back to ctime for birth time, any ordinary write inside `.git` changes the held identity, and pup then refuses every later git spawn in the main checkout as a swapped repo.
findings.body:
**Birth time in the held identity can make pup refuse a repo after its own git writes.**

The identity string now carries `stat.birthtimeMs` for `.git`, `objects/` and `refs/`:

```ts
const of = (stat: Stats | undefined): string =>
  stat ? `${stat.dev}:${stat.ino}:${stat.birthtimeMs}` : 'none';
```

Node's `fs.Stats` docs say that where birth time is unavailable, `birthtime` "may instead hold either the ctime or 1970-01-01". On Linux, libuv tries `statx` first. When that fails with EPERM, ENOSYS, EINVAL or EOPNOTSUPP (for example under a seccomp filter that blocks `statx` in older Docker, on a pre-4.11 kernel, or on some network filesystems), it falls back to `lstat` and copies `st_ctim` into the birth time. These details come from pinned-version knowledge, so confidence is medium.

A directory's ctime changes whenever an entry inside it is created, renamed or removed. That happens on ordinary git activity:
- `index.lock` → `index` and `packed-refs.lock` in `.git`
- a new loose-object fan-out directory in `objects/`
- a new namespace under `refs/`

**Trigger.** Two concrete paths:
- **pup's own write.** `deleteBranchAt` (merge-gate.service.ts:1642) runs `update-ref -d` in a held main checkout and touches `packed-refs.lock`. The new `checkedAfter` then throws `RewrittenGitDirError`. `deleteBranchAt`'s catch swallows it, and every later `runGit` on that repo in the process is refused.
- **The operator's write.** With a long-running `pup ui`, any `git commit` or `git status` the operator runs in the main checkout changes `.git`'s ctime, and pup's next spawn is refused with "restart pup".

Before this PR the identity was dev:ino only, which no git operation changes. The JSDoc above it and ADR 0181 both say the birth time "adds little", so this is a hard break on such hosts (Linux is a supported gate host per ADR 0078) in exchange for little protection.

The fix: drop the birth time. Also drop the birth-time sentences in the JSDoc at L694-698 and in ADR 0181's *The identity* paragraph.

findings.description: ghInCheckout now throws RewrittenGitDirError out of readPullRequestReview, but waitForCiReview's catch-all (ci-wait.service.ts:114-118) treats it as one more wait. pup ci wait therefore keeps polling a refused checkout until --timeout, instead of stopping at once on the refusal. Rethrow RewrittenGitDirError there.

The new GIT_* allowlist keeps GIT_SSL_CAINFO/CAPATH but drops git's other HTTP transport variables (GIT_SSL_CERT, GIT_SSL_KEY, GIT_SSL_NO_VERIFY, GIT_PROXY_SSL_*, GIT_HTTP_PROXY_AUTHMETHOD). Before, these were inherited, so an operator whose HTTPS remote relies on them now sees pushBranch's git push fail with an SSL or auth error.

heldFleet re-implements in src/cli which fleet projects are read (repoExists && isOwnPath && awake-or-shown-dormant), a rule src/core/fleet.service.ts already owns through awakeFleet and fleetRefusal. AGENTS.md says "src/cli/ stays thin; logic lives in src/core/", and the two copies can now drift apart, so heldFleet would check the wrong set.

ADR 181 says every gh spawn is checked before and after through ghInCheckout, but no source-scan guard like decision 172's childProcessUses test covers github.client.ts. A new execFileSync('gh', …) that skips ghInCheckout would therefore pass CI.
assertMainCheckout's JSDoc still says the first call records the identity of ".git and objects/". The identity now covers refs/ too, and it is recorded only once the checks pass.

The new generics checkedAfter<T> (git-diff.client.ts:638) and ghInCheckout<T> (github.client.ts:79) use a bare T, while general.md says "Generics are descriptive — TConfig, TResponse. Never bare T / U".
